result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You fell at home and hit your head. You did not lose consciousness.

Your right hip X-ray shows no fracture (broken bone).

Your head scan (CT) shows no bleeding inside your head.

Your blood pressure was 142/80 lying down. It was 108/66 standing up. This is called postural hypotension (blood pressure drops when you stand up).

Your medicine amlodipine may be making your blood pressure drop when you stand up.

## What you need to do
1. Stand up slowly.
2. Sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before you stand.
3. Wait for the Falls Prevention Clinic to write to you with an appointment. You have been referred.
4. Your GP will recheck your lying and standing blood pressure in 4 weeks.

## Dates and medicines
- 14 October 2026: the date you were seen at the hospital.
- In 4 weeks: your GP will recheck your blood pressure, lying and standing.
- Amlodipine 10 milligrams: STOP this medicine.
- All other medicines: continue them.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- Why might amlodipine cause my blood pressure to drop?
- What will happen at the Falls Prevention Clinic?
- What will my GP check in 4 weeks?

## When to get urgent help
If you get a worsening headache, vomiting, confusion or drowsiness in the next few days, call 999 or go to A&E.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
